guideTitle: 6 Best Threshold Ramps for Sliding Glass Doors in 2026
metaTitle: Best Threshold Ramps for Sliding Glass Doors
metaDescription: Six threshold ramps for sliding glass door tracks compared by gap handling, rise, width and removability, so the door can still slide and lock.
introParagraphs: A sliding glass door is the awkward threshold. The track is a raised metal rail with a recessed channel beside it, the door must keep sliding, and the lip is often just high enough to stop a walker or a small caster. A ramp that works at a hinged door can fail here because it blocks the glide or cannot sit over a hollow channel.

The six picks below take two approaches. Bridge ramps in aluminum span the track and leave the opening clear, and rubber wedges cover or abut the rail from the outside. Which one fits depends on how tall the rail is, how wide the channel is, and whether the door needs to close and lock with the ramp in place.

Measure three things before you shop: the height of the highest rail, the width of the gap in the channel, and the clear space on both sides of the door. A track ramp is steeper than the 1 to 12 slope used for public ramps, so ask an occupational therapist if the person crossing needs more than a small lip lowered.

products.name: Nuvium Bridge Threshold Ramp 27.6 x 17 in, 1.6 in High
products.description:
Nuvium designed this bridge ramp for exactly the sliding door problem. Removable support bars fit openings from 2.8 in to 5.1 in wide, and the ramp measures 27.6 in by 17 in at 1.6 in high. The listing says it suits wheelchairs, walkers, scooters and power chairs on compatible low thresholds.

The key idea is that it spans the track instead of burying it. That keeps the channel open and lets the door slide when the ramp is removed. The support bars must match the real gap, so measure the channel at its widest and narrowest points, and expect to adjust the bars before the first use. The listing does not state a weight rating, so ask before using it with a heavy power chair.

A 1.6 in height covers a typical low rail, not a tall step. It is the only pick here built around a gap, which is why it leads. Against the FinityPro 2 inch, it is lower, simpler and shorter, with less documentation of load.
products.bestFor: A low sliding door with a channel of 2.8 to 5.1 inches that must stay usable.
pros: Spans a track instead of covering it
Support bars fit gaps from 2.8 to 5.1 in
Listed for walkers and power chairs
Compact 27.6 by 17 inch footprint
cons: Capacity is not stated in the listing
Support bars must match the real gap
1.6 inch height limits it to low edges

products.name: FinityPro 2 Inch Aluminum Bridge Door Threshold Ramp
products.description:
FinityPro makes a bridge-type aluminum ramp that adapts to thresholds up to 2 in. It is 29.5 in wide and 27 in long, and a sturdy base plate carries a 5.3 in center section. A five-part adjustable design lets you connect or detach segments to set the height, and the maker lists an 800 lb capacity in anodized aluminum.

The modular parts are useful for a track whose height you are not sure of, or for a door shared by a few heights. At 2 in over a 27 in length the slope is about 1 in 13, close to the 1 to 12 public benchmark, which is far gentler than a rubber wedge. That is a real advantage for a manual chair.

The tradeoff is that segments can come apart or sit out of place, so check them before every use. Aluminum is also louder underfoot than rubber. Compared with the Nuvium bridge ramp, it adds a stated rating, a longer slope and adjustable height, but it covers more floor area.
products.bestFor: A sliding door with a 1 to 2 inch rail where a gentle approach slope is wanted.
pros: Five-part design adjusts to the rail height
27 inch length gives a gentle slope at 2 inches
800 lb capacity is stated in the listing
Anodized aluminum resists rust
cons: Modular segments need checking before each use
Takes more floor area than a short wedge

products.name: FinityPro 3 Inch Aluminum Bridge Door Threshold Ramp
products.description:
This bigger FinityPro bridge ramp measures 37.5 in long and 29.5 in wide and adapts to thresholds up to 3 in. A base plate gives stability, and a 5.3 in center section sets the height. Three configurations are listed, 1 in, 2 in and 3 in, and the capacity is 800 lb in anodized aluminum.

A 3 in setting across 37.5 in is a slope of about 1 in 12.5, which is close to the public benchmark, a rare result for a door ramp. That makes it the gentlest pick here for a tall track or a raised patio door. The cost is footprint, since it needs space inside and outside the door.

Because it sits on top of the track, check that the door can still close with the ramp removed, and that the ramp does not shift when someone steps on it. Next to the FinityPro 2 inch model, it adds height and length, and it is the choice if your rail sits above 2 in.
products.bestFor: A raised patio door where the track and sill add up to about 3 inches.
pros: 37.5 inch length gives about 1 in 12.5 at 3 inches
One kit covers 1, 2 and 3 inch settings
Base plate adds stability on the floor
Anodized aluminum resists rust
cons: Large footprint needs room on both sides
Removable parts need checking each setup

products.name: VEVOR 1.6 Inch Cuttable Natural Rubber Ramp
products.description:
VEVOR sells a 1.6 in solid natural rubber wedge, 35.4 in wide, that is meant to be cut to the width of a threshold. The leftover section can be used elsewhere. The maker calls the rubber heat and wear resistant, and the face is textured for grip.

On a sliding door, a wedge works on the outside of the track, where a patio edge meets the rail, not in the channel itself. It lowers the lip of the exterior step and leaves the door free to slide. The listing gives no run length, so you cannot work out the slope, and the 33069 lb figure is vehicle scale and says little about the shape.

It is a good fit when the channel is narrow or the door sits flush with a patio. Cut slowly with a sharp blade and smooth the cut face. Against the Nuvium bridge ramp, it is simpler but cannot span a gap.
products.bestFor: A patio door where the outside lip is a solid edge and the track must stay clear.
pros: Cuts to the exact width of the sill
Leftover piece can serve a second door
Solid natural rubber resists wear
Textured face adds grip when wet
cons: Run length is missing from the listing
Cutting takes a careful measure first

products.name: Nuvium 1 Inch Rise Rubber Threshold Ramp
products.description:
Nuvium offers a dense natural rubber wedge sized 1 in by 5.3 in by 35.5 in, with a 2000 lb rating and deep grooves. It is meant for raised door sills and small steps indoors or outdoors. A mild rubber odor or a slight curve may be present when it arrives.

For a sliding door, think of it as a patio-side wedge. It covers a 1 in drop to the deck or the inside floor, not the track channel. The 5.3 in run makes a slope of about 1 in 5.3, steep in ratio but small in height. The 35.5 in width spans the door opening, so the wheels never find an exposed edge.

It is quiet and holds its position well on a clean floor. Compared with the VEVOR, it is a fixed size with no cutting but states its numbers. It cannot replace a bridge ramp where a hollow channel runs under the wheels.
products.bestFor: A one inch drop between a patio and the door track that is not a hollow channel.
pros: Wide 35.5 inch span covers a standard doorway
Deep grooves add grip on a wet or dry surface
2000 lb rating leaves ample margin for devices
Dense natural rubber suits indoor or outdoor use
cons: Short 5.3 inch run makes a steep slope
Listing mentions a mild rubber odor on arrival
Slight curve may need time to flatten out

products.name: Heonay Self-Adhesive Rubber Threshold Ramp
products.description:
Heonay offers a rubber strip with an adhesive backing that goes down without nails or glue. Grooves in the surface channel water and add traction, and the rubber is chosen for its resistance to being crushed. The listing text gives no rise, run or rating.

For sliding doors the adhesive base is a double-edged feature. It stops the strip from creeping when the door is used, but it also makes the ramp close to permanent. It will not span a gap, and a track that still has to be cleaned or serviced may be harder to reach once strips are stuck beside it. Check which surface the adhesive will touch.

It suits a patio edge or an interior floor lip next to a track, not the track itself. Next to the Nuvium wedge, you give up published numbers for a locked-down position.
products.bestFor: A smooth interior floor edge beside a track where a loose wedge keeps moving.
pros: Adhesive backing keeps it from sliding
Goes down with no nails, glue or tools
Grooves create drainage paths for water
Compression-resistant rubber keeps its shape
cons: Rise and capacity are missing from the listing

buyingCriteria.explanation: A sliding door has a raised rail and a channel beside it. Measure the highest rail from the floor and the gap across the channel at several points. The Nuvium bridge ramp fits 2.8 to 5.1 in gaps at 1.6 in high, and the FinityPro models adapt to rails up to 2 in or 3 in. A wedge only fits if there is a solid surface to rest on.

A bridge spans the channel and can be lifted away, so the door can still close. A wedge covers a solid lip, as the VEVOR 1.6 inch and Nuvium 1 inch do. Using a wedge over a hollow track can crush the track or leave a gap under the wheel. Match the shape to what is under the wheel path.

A ramp that stays in the track blocks the door from closing or locking. Bridge ramps like the Nuvium or FinityPro can be removed at night. Adhesive strips like the Heonay stay put. Think about security and weather sealing before you commit to a fixed ramp.

The FinityPro 3 inch at 37.5 in is about 1 in 12.5 at 3 in, the FinityPro 2 inch at 27 in is about 1 in 13 at 2 in, and the Nuvium 1 inch is about 1 in 5.3. Longer ramps are gentler. The 1 to 12 public benchmark is a useful yardstick.
The FinityPro models list 800 lb and the Nuvium 1 inch lists 2000 lb. The Nuvium bridge and Heonay list none. Add up the user, device and carried items, and ask when a number is missing.

The FinityPro 3 inch measures 37.5 by 29.5 in, the Nuvium bridge 27.6 by 17 in, and the rubber wedges are slim. A big bridge needs clear floor on both sides of the track. Measure the space before you decide.

howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each ramp can span a channel. The Nuvium bridge ramp and both FinityPro ramps do, while the rubber wedges and Heonay strip only cover solid lips. Based on product specs and buyer feedback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rise coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 1.6 inches for the Nuvium bridge, up to 2 inches and 3 inches for the FinityPro models, and 1 inch to 1.6 inches for the rubber wedges.

howWeEvaluated.title: Slope from stated size
howWeEvaluated.description: We divided rise by length where both were given, such as the FinityPro 2 inch at 27 inches and the Nuvium wedge at 5.3 inches. Where run was missing, we said so.

howWeEvaluated.title: Removability
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored ramps that lift away so the door can close, led by the bridge designs, and noted the near-permanent adhesive on the Heonay.

faq.q: Can I put a rubber wedge over a sliding door track?
faq.a: Only if the track is solid underneath. A hollow channel can leave the wedge unsupported or crush the track. A bridge such as the Nuvium Bridge ramp is made for gaps from 2.8 to 5.1 in.

faq.q: Will the door still close with the ramp in place?
faq.a: Not with a fixed ramp on the track. Bridge ramps lift away, so you can remove them at night. An adhesive strip like the Heonay stays in place, so check clearance first.

faq.q: How do I measure the gap?
faq.a: Measure the channel width at the narrowest and widest points and the height of the highest rail. The Nuvium bridge bars fit 2.8 to 5.1 in. Measure twice, since tracks vary, and measure again after cleaning out any dirt or old weatherstripping, which can hide a quarter inch of extra width in the channel and change which support bar setting fits.

faq.q: Which ramp has the gentlest slope?
faq.a: The FinityPro 3 inch, at 37.5 in long, is about 1 in 12.5 at 3 in. The FinityPro 2 inch is about 1 in 13 at 2 in. Rubber wedges are about 1 in 5.

The listings describe anodized aluminum and modular parts, but we have not measured grip. Keep the surface dry and clean, and check that it does not slide. Press down on each corner and the center after setting it, and look for a rocking edge on a slightly uneven patio floor, which is common near a door track.

faq.q: Does the VEVOR rating of 33069 lb matter?
faq.a: It is vehicle scale and says little about wheelchair use. Check that the user and device are well under any listed rating, and look at the shape and rise instead.

faq.q: When should I ask a professional?
faq.a: If the rail is over 3 inches, the user needs help to cross, or the door is a main entrance, ask an occupational therapist or an installer. Bring photos of the track and the measurements of rail height, gap width and clear floor on both sides, since sliding door frames differ a great deal and a quick look at the real opening saves a wrong purchase. A therapist can also advise on whether a ramp or a different door style suits the person.
